   178→
   179→def _resolve_inputs(
   180→    opts: QueueBuildOptions, state: StateModel,
   181→) -> tuple[dict | None, str | None, str, float]:
   182→    """Resolve plan, scan_path, status, and subjective threshold from options."""
   183→    ctx = opts.context
   184→    plan = ctx.plan if ctx is not None else opts.plan
   185→
   186→    scan_path: str | None = (
   187→        state.get("scan_path")
   188→        if isinstance(opts.scan_path, _ScanPathFromState)
   189→        else opts.scan_path
   190→    )
   191→
   192→    status = opts.status
   193→    if status not in ALL_STATUSES:
   194→        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported status filter: {status}")
   195→
   196→    try:
   197→        threshold = float(opts.subjective_threshold)
   198→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
   199→        threshold = 100.0
   200→    threshold = max(0.0, min(100.0, threshold))
   201→
   202→    return plan, scan_path, status, threshold
   203→
   204→
   205→def _gather_subjective_items(
   206→    state: StateModel,
   207→    opts: QueueBuildOptions,
   208→    threshold: float,
   209→) -> list[WorkQueueItem]:
   210→    """Build subjective dimension candidates.
   211→
   212→    Lifecycle filtering (endgame gating) happens in ``apply_lifecycle_filter``,
   213→    not here. This function only handles configuration and scope.
   214→    """
   215→    if not opts.include_subjective:
   216→        return []
   217→    if opts.status not in {"open", "all"}:
   218→        return []
   219→    if opts.chronic:
   220→        return []
   221→
   222→    candidates = build_subjective_items(
   223→        state, state.get("issues", {}), threshold=threshold,
   224→    )
   225→    return [item for item in candidates if scope_matches(item, opts.scope)]
   226→
   227→
   228→def _gather_workflow_items(
   229→    state: StateModel, plan: dict | None, status: str,
   230→) -> list[WorkQueueItem]:
   231→    """Inject triage stages, checkpoints, and create-plan when plan is active."""
   232→    if not plan or status not in {"open", "all"}:
   233→        return []
   234→
   235→    items: list[WorkQueueItem] = []
   236→    for builder in (build_deferred_disposition_item, build_run_scan_item):
   237→        item = builder(plan)
   238→        if item is not None:
   239→            items.append(item)
   240→    items.extend(build_triage_stage_items(plan, state))
   241→    for builder in (
   242→        build_score_checkpoint_item,
   243→        build_import_scores_item,
   244→        build_communicate_score_item,
   245→    ):
   246→        item = builder(plan, state)
   247→        if item is not None:
   248→            items.append(item)
   249→    plan_item = build_create_plan_item(plan)
   250→    if plan_item is not None:
   251→        items.append(plan_item)
   252→    return items
   253→
   254→
   255→def _planned_item_ids(plan: dict) -> set[str]:
   256→    """Collect IDs explicitly tracked by the living plan."""
   257→    tracked_ids: set[str] = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
   258→    tracked_ids.update(plan.get("skipped", {}).keys())
   259→    tracked_ids.update(plan.get("overrides", {}).keys())
   260→    for cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).values():
   261→        tracked_ids.update(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   262→        for step in cluster.get("action_steps", []):
   263→            if isinstance(step, dict):
   264→                tracked_ids.update(step.get("issue_refs", []))
   265→    subjective_defer_meta = plan.get("subjective_defer_meta", {})
   266→    if isinstance(subjective_defer_meta, dict):
   267→        tracked_ids.update(subjective_defer_meta.get("force_visible_ids", []))
   268→    return tracked_ids
   269→
   270→
   271→def _filter_plan_visibility(
   272→    items: list[WorkQueueItem],
   273→    plan: dict | None,
   274→    *,
   275→    visibility: str,
   276→) -> list[WorkQueueItem]:
   277→    """Apply plan-based visibility filtering for execution/backlog surfaces."""
   278→    if visibility == QueueVisibility.ALL:
   279→        return items
   280→    if not plan:
   281→        return items
   282→    tracked_ids = _planned_item_ids(plan)
   283→    if not tracked_ids:
   284→        if visibility == QueueVisibility.EXECUTION:
   285→            return [item for item in items if _is_implicit_execution_workflow(item)]
   286→        return items
   287→    if visibility == QueueVisibility.EXECUTION:
   288→        return [
   289→            item for item in items
   290→            if item["id"] in tracked_ids or _is_implicit_execution_workflow(item)
   291→        ]
   292→    if visibility == QueueVisibility.BACKLOG:
   293→        return [
   294→            item for item in items
   295→            if item["id"] not in tracked_ids and not _is_implicit_execution_workflow(item)
   296→        ]
   297→    return items
   298→
   299→
   300→def _is_implicit_execution_workflow(item: WorkQueueItem) -> bool:
   301→    """Return True for workflow items that opt into execution visibility."""
   302→    return (
   303→        item.get("kind") == "workflow_action"
   304→        and item.get("execution_visibility") == "always"
   305→    )
   306→
   307→
   308→
   309→def _plan_presort(
   310→    items: list[WorkQueueItem], state: StateModel, plan: dict | None,
   311→) -> tuple[set[str], list[WorkQueueItem]]:
   312→    """Enrich plan metadata and stamp sort keys before sorting.
   313→
   314→    Returns ``(new_ids, skipped)`` — skipped items are removed from
   315→    ``items`` in place and returned separately for post-sort re-append.
   316→    """
   317→    if not plan:
   318→        return set(), []
   319→
   320→    new_ids = _new_item_ids(state)
   321→    enrich_plan_metadata(items, plan)
   322→    stamp_plan_sort_keys(items, plan, new_ids)
   323→    remaining, skipped = separate_skipped(items, plan)
   324→    items[:] = remaining
   325→    return new_ids, skipped
   326→
   327→
   328→def _plan_postsort(
   329→    items: list[WorkQueueItem],
   330→    skipped: list[WorkQueueItem],
   331→    plan: dict | None,
   332→    opts: QueueBuildOptions,
   333→) -> None:
   334→    """Re-append skipped items and stamp positions.
   335→
   336→    Cluster focus filtering is intentionally NOT applied here — it is a
   337→    view-layer concern that callers apply after building the canonical queue.
   338→    This prevents UI focus state from affecting lifecycle decisions (scan
   339→    gating, score display mode, empty-queue fallback).
   340→    """
   341→    if not plan:
   342→        return
   343→
   344→    if opts.include_skipped:
   345→        items.extend(skipped)
   346→    stamp_positions(items, plan)
   347→

Perfect! Now I have all the information I need. Let me create a comprehensive summary.

Based on my thorough analysis of the codebase, here's exactly how auto-clusters get inserted into the execution queue and what would need to change to make them go to backlog instead:

## How Auto-Clusters Currently Get Added to the Execution Queue

### 1. **Cluster Creation vs. Queue Membership Are Separate**

Auto-clusters are created in `desloppify/engine/_plan/auto_cluster_sync_issue.py` via `_sync_auto_cluster()`, which:
- **Creates the cluster object** in `plan["clusters"][cluster_name]`
- **Sets cluster members** via `cluster["issue_ids"]`
- **Creates override entries** for each member in `plan["overrides"][issue_id]` pointing back to the cluster

**Critically**: Creating a cluster does NOT automatically add members to `plan["queue_order"]`. The cluster and its members are just catalogued in the plan's data structures.

### 2. **Queue Membership is Determined by `queue_order` and `overrides`, Not Cluster Membership**

The execution queue vs. backlog split happens in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/core.py` at lines 271-297 in `_filter_plan_visibility()`:

```python
def _filter_plan_visibility(items, plan, visibility=visibility):
    tracked_ids = _planned_item_ids(plan)  # Collects from:
    # - plan["queue_order"]
    # - plan["skipped"]
    # - plan["overrides"]
    # - cluster["issue_ids"] for all clusters
    
    if visibility == QueueVisibility.EXECUTION:
        return [item for item in items 
                if item["id"] in tracked_ids or _is_implicit_execution_workflow(item)]
    if visibility == QueueVisibility.BACKLOG:
        return [item for item in items
                if item["id"] not in tracked_ids and not _is_implicit_execution_workflow(item)]
```

**An item appears in the execution queue if:**
1. Its ID is in `plan["queue_order"]`, OR
2. Its ID is in `plan["skipped"]` (skipped items are still "tracked"), OR  
3. Its ID is in an `override["cluster"]` reference, OR
4. Its ID is in `cluster["issue_ids"]` for ANY cluster in `plan["clusters"]`

**An item appears in the backlog if:** none of the above are true.

### 3. **How Members Get Into Queue Display (via `collapse_clusters()`)**

When rendering, `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/plan_order.py` lines 218-280 in `collapse_clusters()`:
- Maps each issue ID to its cluster (if any)
- **For clusters with 2+ members in the visible queue**: collapses them into a single "cluster" meta-item
- **Auto-clusters collapse in-place** where the first member appears
- **Manual clusters** are moved to the front in plan order

But this is just DISPLAY collapsing—it doesn't determine queue membership.

### 4. **Where Auto-Cluster Members Actually Get Into `queue_order`**

Auto-clusters create **overrides** for their members at lines 155-161 in `auto_cluster_sync_issue.py`:

```python
overrides = plan.get("overrides", {})
for fid in member_ids:
    if fid not in overrides:
        overrides[fid] = {"issue_id": fid, "created_at": now}
    overrides[fid]["cluster"] = current_name
    overrides[fid]["updated_at"] = now
```

The `override` entry doesn't put the ID in `queue_order`; it just marks cluster ownership. **However**, having an override makes the ID part of `tracked_ids` in `_planned_item_ids()`, which includes it in the execution queue.

## Critical Finding: **There IS No Automatic Queue Insertion**

When I searched for code that adds cluster members to `queue_order` after cluster creation, I found **nothing**. Auto-cluster members are:
1. Added to `cluster["issue_ids"]`
2. Added to `overrides` with cluster references
3. **NOT** explicitly added to `queue_order`

Yet they appear in the execution queue because `_planned_item_ids()` counts members of ANY cluster as "tracked", regardless of whether they're in `queue_order`.

In `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/core.py` line 255-268, modify `_planned_item_ids()` to NOT include cluster member IDs:

```python
def _planned_item_ids(plan):
    tracked_ids = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
    tracked_ids.update(plan.get("skipped", {}).keys())
    tracked_ids.update(plan.get("overrides", {}).keys())
    # REMOVE THIS:
    # for cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).values():
    #     tracked_ids.update(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
    # ...rest unchanged
```

This would cause cluster members to be backlog-only unless explicitly in `queue_order`.

**Option 2: Don't create override entries (Breaking)**

Modify `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/auto_cluster_sync_issue.py` lines 155-161 to NOT create overrides. But this would break cluster UI rendering that depends on `override["cluster"]` to find cluster membership.

**Option 3: Only mark auto-clusters as backlog**

When syncing auto-clusters, instead of just creating overrides, selectively add members to `queue_order`:

```

    20→    position: str,
    21→    target: str | None = None,
    22→    offset: int | None = None,
    23→    issue_ids: list[str] | None = None,
    24→) -> int:
    25→    """Resolve a position specifier to an insertion index.
    26→
    27→    ``issue_ids`` are the IDs being moved — used to calculate relative
    28→    positions when they already exist in the list.

    30→    moving = set(issue_ids or [])
    31→
    32→    if position == "top":
    33→        return 0
    34→    if position == "bottom":
    35→        return len(order)
    36→
    37→    if position in {"before", "after"} and target:
    38→        return _resolve_relative_position(order, moving, position=position, target=target)
    39→
    40→    if position in {"up", "down"} and offset is not None:
    41→        return _resolve_offset_position(

    43→            moving,
    44→            position=position,
    45→            offset=offset,
    46→            issue_ids=issue_ids,
    47→        )
    48→
    49→    return len(order)
    50→
    51→
    52→def _resolve_relative_position(
    53→    order: list[str],
    54→    moving: set[str],
    55→    *,
    56→    position: str,
    57→    target: str,
    58→) -> int:
    59→    for i, item_id in enumerate(order):
    60→        if item_id == target and item_id not in moving:
    61→            return i if position == "before" else i + 1
    62→    return 0 if position == "before" else len(order)
    63→

    65→def _find_index(items: list[str], target: str) -> int | None:
    66→    for i, item_id in enumerate(items):
    67→        if item_id == target:
    68→            return i
    69→    return None
    70→

    72→def _resolve_offset_position(
    73→    order: list[str],
    74→    moving: set[str],
    75→    *,
    76→    position: str,

    78→    issue_ids: list[str] | None,

    82→    first_id = issue_ids[0]

     5→from desloppify.base.config import DEFAULT_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE
     6→from desloppify.engine._plan.constants import AUTO_PREFIX
     7→from desloppify.engine._plan.auto_cluster_sync import (
     8→    prune_stale_clusters as _prune_stale_clusters,
     9→    sync_issue_clusters as _sync_issue_clusters,
    10→    sync_subjective_clusters as _sync_subjective_clusters,
    11→)
    12→from desloppify.engine._plan.schema import PlanModel, ensure_plan_defaults
    13→from desloppify.engine._plan.policy.subjective import SubjectiveVisibility
    14→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import StateModel, utc_now
    15→
    16→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    17→# Repair
    18→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    19→
    20→def _repair_ghost_cluster_refs(plan: PlanModel, now: str) -> int:
    21→    """Cross-check cluster membership between cluster.issue_ids and overrides.
    22→
    23→    Repairs three kinds of drift:
    24→    1. Override points to a cluster that does not exist → clear override.
    25→    2. Override points to cluster X, but issue is not in X's issue_ids → add it.
    26→    3. Issue is in cluster.issue_ids but override points elsewhere (or has no
    27→       cluster ref) → update override to match cluster.issue_ids.
    28→
    29→    cluster.issue_ids is treated as authoritative when it disagrees with
    30→    the override, because the sync helpers always write issue_ids first.
    31→    """
    32→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
    33→    overrides = plan.get("overrides", {})
    34→    repaired = 0
    35→
    36→    # Direction 1: override → cluster that doesn't exist
    37→    for override in overrides.values():
    38→        cluster_name = override.get("cluster")
    39→        if cluster_name and cluster_name not in clusters:
    40→            override["cluster"] = None
    41→            override["updated_at"] = now
    42→            repaired += 1
    43→
    44→    # Build authoritative map: issue_id → cluster_name from cluster.issue_ids.
    45→    # When an issue appears in multiple clusters, prefer manual (non-auto)
    46→    # clusters, matching the priority in collapse_clusters.
    47→    canonical: dict[str, str] = {}
    48→    for name, cluster in clusters.items():
    49→        for issue_id in cluster.get("issue_ids", []):
    50→            if issue_id not in canonical or not cluster.get("auto"):
    51→                canonical[issue_id] = name
    52→
    53→    # Direction 2+3: ensure overrides agree with cluster.issue_ids
    54→    for issue_id, cluster_name in canonical.items():
    55→        override = overrides.get(issue_id)
    56→        if override is None:
    57→            overrides[issue_id] = {
    58→                "issue_id": issue_id,
    59→                "cluster": cluster_name,
    60→                "created_at": now,
    61→                "updated_at": now,
    62→            }
    63→            repaired += 1
    64→        elif override.get("cluster") != cluster_name:
    65→            override["cluster"] = cluster_name
    66→            override["updated_at"] = now
    67→            repaired += 1
    68→
    69→    # Direction 2 (reverse): override says cluster X, but issue not in X.issue_ids.
    70→    # If the issue isn't in *any* cluster's issue_ids, clear the override ref.
    71→    for issue_id, override in overrides.items():
    72→        ref = override.get("cluster")
    73→        if not ref or ref not in clusters:
    74→            continue
    75→        if issue_id in canonical:
    76→            continue  # already handled above
    77→        # Override points to a real cluster, but issue is not in any
    78→        # cluster's issue_ids → stale ref, clear it.
    79→        override["cluster"] = None
    80→        override["updated_at"] = now
    81→        repaired += 1
    82→
    83→    return repaired
    84→
    85→
    86→def auto_cluster_issues(
    87→    plan: PlanModel,
    88→    state: StateModel,
    89→    *,
    90→    target_strict: float = DEFAULT_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE,
    91→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
    92→) -> int:
    93→    """Regenerate auto-clusters from current open issues.
    94→
    95→    Returns count of changes made (clusters created, updated, or deleted).
    96→    """
    97→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
    98→
    99→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
   100→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   101→
   102→    # Map existing auto-clusters by cluster_key
   103→    existing_by_key: dict[str, str] = {}  # cluster_key → cluster_name
   104→    for name, cluster in list(clusters.items()):
   105→        if cluster.get("auto"):
   106→            ck = cluster.get("cluster_key", "")
   107→            if ck:
   108→                existing_by_key[ck] = name
   109→
   110→    now = utc_now()
   111→    active_auto_keys: set[str] = set()
   112→    changes = 0
   113→
   114→    changes += _sync_issue_clusters(
   115→        plan, issues, clusters, existing_by_key, active_auto_keys, now,
   116→    )
   117→    changes += _sync_subjective_clusters(
   118→        plan, state, issues, clusters, existing_by_key, active_auto_keys, now,
   119→        target_strict=target_strict,
   120→        policy=policy,
   121→    )
   122→    changes += _prune_stale_clusters(
   123→        plan, issues, clusters, active_auto_keys, now,
   124→    )
   125→    changes += _repair_ghost_cluster_refs(plan, now)
   126→
   127→    plan["updated"] = now
   128→    return changes
   129→
   130→
   131→__all__ = [
   132→    "AUTO_PREFIX",
   133→    "auto_cluster_issues",
   134→]
   135→

1→"""Issue auto-cluster synchronization helpers."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from collections import defaultdict
     6→from dataclasses import dataclass
     7→
     8→from desloppify.base.registry import DETECTORS
     9→from desloppify.engine._plan.cluster_strategy import (
    10→    cluster_name_from_key as _cluster_name_from_key,

    12→from desloppify.engine._plan.cluster_strategy import (

    16→    generate_description as _generate_description,
    17→)
    18→from desloppify.engine._plan.cluster_strategy import (
    19→    grouping_key as _grouping_key,
    20→)
    21→
    22→_MIN_CLUSTER_SIZE = 2
    23→
    24→
    25→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    26→class AutoClusterSyncResult:
    27→    """Explicit result describing what `_sync_auto_cluster` changed."""
    28→
    29→    cluster_name: str
    30→    changed: bool
    31→    created: bool
    32→    member_count: int
    33→
    34→
    35→def _manual_member_ids(clusters: dict) -> set[str]:
    36→    """Collect all issue IDs belonging to manual (non-auto) clusters."""
    37→    ids: set[str] = set()
    38→    for cluster in clusters.values():
    39→        if not cluster.get("auto"):
    40→            ids.update(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
    41→    return ids
    42→
    43→
    44→def _group_clusterable_issues(
    45→    issues: dict,
    46→    *,
    47→    manual_member_ids: set[str],
    48→) -> tuple[dict[str, list[str]], dict[str, dict]]:
    49→    """Group open, non-suppressed, non-manual issues by detector/subtype key."""
    50→    groups: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
    51→    issue_data: dict[str, dict] = {}
    52→    for fid, issue in issues.items():
    53→        if issue.get("status") != "open":
    54→            continue
    55→        if issue.get("suppressed"):
    56→            continue
    57→        if fid in manual_member_ids:
    58→            continue
    59→
    60→        detector = issue.get("detector", "")
    61→        meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
    62→        key = _grouping_key(issue, meta)
    63→        if key is None:
    64→            continue
    65→
    66→        groups[key].append(fid)
    67→        issue_data[fid] = issue
    68→
    69→    groups = {k: v for k, v in groups.items() if len(v) >= _MIN_CLUSTER_SIZE}
    70→    return groups, issue_data
    71→
    72→
    73→def _sync_user_modified_cluster_members(
    74→    plan: dict,
    75→    *,
    76→    clusters: dict,
    77→    existing_name: str,
    78→    member_ids: list[str],
    79→    now: str,
    80→) -> int:
    81→    """Sync member IDs for a user-modified cluster, returns count of changes."""
    82→    cluster = clusters[existing_name]
    83→    changes = 0
    84→    existing_ids = set(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
    85→    new_ids = [fid for fid in member_ids if fid not in existing_ids]
    86→    if new_ids:
    87→        cluster["issue_ids"].extend(new_ids)
    88→        cluster["updated_at"] = now
    89→        changes = 1
    90→    overrides = plan.get("overrides", {})
    91→    for fid in member_ids:
    92→        if fid not in overrides:
    93→            overrides[fid] = {"issue_id": fid, "created_at": now}
    94→        overrides[fid]["cluster"] = existing_name
    95→        overrides[fid]["updated_at"] = now
    96→    return changes
    97→
    98→
    99→def _sync_auto_cluster(
   100→    plan: dict,
   101→    clusters: dict,
   102→    existing_by_key: dict[str, str],
   103→    *,
   104→    cluster_key: str,
   105→    cluster_name: str,
   106→    member_ids: list[str],
   107→    description: str,
   108→    action: str,
   109→    now: str,
   110→    optional: bool = False,
   111→) -> AutoClusterSyncResult:
   112→    """Create/update one auto-cluster and report the mutation outcome.
   113→
   114→    Mutates:
   115→      - ``clusters`` (cluster create/update),
   116→      - ``existing_by_key`` (cluster-key to name binding),
   117→      - ``plan['overrides']`` (cluster ownership for each member issue).
   118→    """
   119→    changes = 0
   120→    created = False
   121→    existing_name = existing_by_key.get(cluster_key)
   122→    if existing_name and existing_name in clusters:
   123→        cluster = clusters[existing_name]
   124→        old_ids = set(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   125→        new_ids_set = set(member_ids)
   126→        if (
   127→            old_ids != new_ids_set
   128→            or cluster.get("description") != description
   129→            or cluster.get("action") != action
   130→        ):
   131→            cluster["issue_ids"] = list(member_ids)
   132→            cluster["description"] = description
   133→            cluster["action"] = action
   134→            cluster["updated_at"] = now
   135→            changes = 1
   136→    else:
   137→        new_cluster = {
   138→            "name": cluster_name,
   139→            "description": description,
   140→            "issue_ids": list(member_ids),
   141→            "created_at": now,
   142→            "updated_at": now,
   143→            "auto": True,
   144→            "cluster_key": cluster_key,
   145→            "action": action,
   146→            "user_modified": False,
   147→        }
   148→        if optional:
   149→            new_cluster["optional"] = True
   150→        clusters[cluster_name] = new_cluster
   151→        existing_by_key[cluster_key] = cluster_name
   152→        changes = 1
   153→        created = True
   154→
   155→    overrides = plan.get("overrides", {})
   156→    current_name = existing_by_key.get(cluster_key, cluster_name)
   157→    for fid in member_ids:
   158→        if fid not in overrides:
   159→            overrides[fid] = {"issue_id": fid, "created_at": now}
   160→        overrides[fid]["cluster"] = current_name
   161→        overrides[fid]["updated_at"] = now
   162→
   163→    return AutoClusterSyncResult(
   164→        cluster_name=current_name,
   165→        changed=bool(changes),
   166→        created=created,
   167→        member_count=len(member_ids),
   168→    )
   169→
   170→
   171→def sync_issue_clusters(
   172→    plan: dict,
   173→    issues: dict,
   174→    clusters: dict,
   175→    existing_by_key: dict[str, str],
   176→    active_auto_keys: set[str],
   177→    now: str,
   178→) -> int:
   179→    """Group open issues by detector/subtype and sync auto-clusters."""
   180→    changes = 0
   181→
   182→    groups, issue_data = _group_clusterable_issues(
   183→        issues, manual_member_ids=_manual_member_ids(clusters)
   184→    )
   185→
   186→    for key, member_ids in groups.items():
   187→        active_auto_keys.add(key)
   188→        cluster_name = _cluster_name_from_key(key)
   189→
   190→        rep = issue_data.get(member_ids[0], {})
   191→        detector = rep.get("detector", "")
   192→        meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
   193→        members = [issue_data[fid] for fid in member_ids if fid in issue_data]
   194→
   195→        key_parts = key.split("::")
   196→        subtype = key_parts[2] if len(key_parts) >= 3 else None
   197→
   198→        description = _generate_description(cluster_name, members, meta, subtype)
   199→        action = _generate_action(meta, subtype)
   200→
   201→        existing_name = existing_by_key.get(key)
   202→        if existing_name and existing_name in clusters:
   203→            cluster = clusters[existing_name]
   204→            if cluster.get("user_modified"):
   205→                changes += _sync_user_modified_cluster_members(
   206→                    plan,
   207→                    clusters=clusters,
   208→                    existing_name=existing_name,
   209→                    member_ids=member_ids,
   210→                    now=now,
   211→                )
   212→                continue
   213→
   214→        if cluster_name in clusters and clusters[cluster_name].get("cluster_key") != key:
   215→            cluster_name = f"{cluster_name}-{len(member_ids)}"
   216→
   217→        sync_result = _sync_auto_cluster(
   218→            plan,
   219→            clusters,
   220→            existing_by_key,
   221→            cluster_key=key,
   222→            cluster_name=cluster_name,
   223→            member_ids=member_ids,
   224→            description=description,
   225→            action=action,
   226→            now=now,
   227→        )
   228→        changes += int(sync_result.changed)
   229→
   230→    return changes
   231→
   232→
   233→__all__ = ["AutoClusterSyncResult", "sync_issue_clusters"]

   232→def validate_plan(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   233→    """Raise ValueError when plan invariants are violated."""
   234→    if not isinstance(plan.get("version"), int):
   235→        raise ValueError("plan.version must be an int")
   236→    if not isinstance(plan.get("queue_order"), list):
   237→        raise ValueError("plan.queue_order must be a list")
   238→
   239→    # No ID should appear in both queue_order and skipped
   240→    skipped_ids = set(plan.get("skipped", {}).keys())
   241→    overlap = set(plan["queue_order"]) & skipped_ids
   242→    if overlap:
   243→        raise ValueError(
   244→            f"IDs cannot appear in both queue_order and skipped: {sorted(overlap)}"
   245→        )
   246→
   247→    # Validate skip entry kinds
   248→    for fid, entry in plan.get("skipped", {}).items():
   249→        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
   250→            raise ValueError(f"plan.skipped[{fid!r}] must be an object")
   251→        if "kind" not in entry:
   252→            raise ValueError(f"plan.skipped[{fid!r}] missing required key 'kind'")
   253→        kind = entry["kind"]
   254→        if kind not in VALID_SKIP_KINDS:
   255→            raise ValueError(
   256→                f"Invalid skip kind {kind!r} for {fid}; must be one of {sorted(VALID_SKIP_KINDS)}"
   257→            )

1→"""Canonical queue mutation helpers for plan operations."""

     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from desloppify.engine._plan.promoted_ids import add_promoted_ids
     6→from desloppify.engine._plan.schema import PlanModel, SkipEntry, ensure_plan_defaults
     7→
     8→
     9→def _remove_id_from_lists(plan: PlanModel, issue_id: str) -> None:
    10→    """Remove an issue ID from queue_order and skipped."""
    11→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
    12→    skipped: dict[str, SkipEntry] = plan.get("skipped", {})
    13→    if issue_id in order:
    14→        order.remove(issue_id)
    15→    skipped.pop(issue_id, None)
    16→
    17→
    18→def _resolve_position(
    19→    order: list[str],
    20→    position: str,
    21→    target: str | None = None,
    22→    offset: int | None = None,
    23→    issue_ids: list[str] | None = None,
    24→) -> int:
    25→    """Resolve a position specifier to an insertion index.
    26→
    27→    ``issue_ids`` are the IDs being moved — used to calculate relative
    28→    positions when they already exist in the list.
    29→    """
    30→    moving = set(issue_ids or [])
    31→
    32→    if position == "top":
    33→        return 0
    34→    if position == "bottom":
    35→        return len(order)
    36→
    37→    if position in {"before", "after"} and target:
    38→        return _resolve_relative_position(order, moving, position=position, target=target)
    39→
    40→    if position in {"up", "down"} and offset is not None:
    41→        return _resolve_offset_position(
    42→            order,
    43→            moving,
    44→            position=position,
    45→            offset=offset,
    46→            issue_ids=issue_ids,
    47→        )
    48→
    49→    return len(order)
    50→
    51→
    52→def _resolve_relative_position(
    53→    order: list[str],
    54→    moving: set[str],
    55→    *,
    56→    position: str,
    57→    target: str,
    58→) -> int:
    59→    for i, item_id in enumerate(order):
    60→        if item_id == target and item_id not in moving:
    61→            return i if position == "before" else i + 1
    62→    return 0 if position == "before" else len(order)
    63→
    64→
    65→def _find_index(items: list[str], target: str) -> int | None:
    66→    for i, item_id in enumerate(items):
    67→        if item_id == target:
    68→            return i
    69→    return None
    70→
    71→
    72→def _resolve_offset_position(
    73→    order: list[str],
    74→    moving: set[str],
    75→    *,
    76→    position: str,
    77→    offset: int,
    78→    issue_ids: list[str] | None,
    79→) -> int:
    80→    if not issue_ids:
    81→        return 0 if position == "up" else len(order)
    82→    first_id = issue_ids[0]
    83→    clean_order = [x for x in order if x not in moving]
    84→    current_idx = _find_index(clean_order, first_id)
    85→    if current_idx is None:
    86→        if position == "up":
    87→            return max(0, len(clean_order) - offset)
    88→        return len(clean_order)
    89→    if position == "up":
    90→        return max(0, current_idx - offset)
    91→    return min(len(clean_order), current_idx + offset)
    92→
    93→
    94→def move_items(
    95→    plan: PlanModel,
    96→    issue_ids: list[str],
    97→    position: str,
    98→    target: str | None = None,
    99→    offset: int | None = None,
   100→) -> int:
   101→    """Move issue IDs to a position in queue_order. Returns count moved."""
   102→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   103→
   104→    # Triage stage IDs are workflow-managed and cannot be manually reordered.
   105→    from desloppify.engine._plan.constants import TRIAGE_IDS
   106→
   107→    issue_ids = [fid for fid in issue_ids if fid not in TRIAGE_IDS]
   108→    if not issue_ids:
   109→        return 0
   110→
   111→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   112→
   113→    # Remove from skipped if present.
   114→    skipped: dict[str, SkipEntry] = plan.get("skipped", {})
   115→    for fid in issue_ids:
   116→        skipped.pop(fid, None)
   117→
   118→    # Remove from current position in order.
   119→    for fid in issue_ids:
   120→        if fid in order:
   121→            order.remove(fid)
   122→
   123→    # Resolve insertion point.
   124→    idx = _resolve_position(order, position, target, offset, issue_ids)
   125→
   126→    # Insert in original order.
   127→    for i, fid in enumerate(issue_ids):
   128→        order.insert(idx + i, fid)
   129→
   130→    # Track user-promoted IDs only when explicitly moved to the front.
   131→    # Moving to bottom/down/after should not create a promotion barrier.
   132→    if position == "top":
   133→        add_promoted_ids(plan, issue_ids)
   134→
   135→    return len(issue_ids)
   136→
   137→
   138→__all__ = ["move_items", "_remove_id_from_lists"]
   139→

Perfect. Now I have enough context. Let me create a comprehensive summary document. Since this is read-only mode, I'll compile my findings into a clear response for the user.

## Summary: Queue Progression, Scoring, and Backlog Dynamics

Based on my analysis of the desloppify codebase, here are the detailed answers to your questions:

---

### 1. **How "Queue Cleared" / Progression is Determined**

Queue progression happens through the **lifecycle phase system** (`desloppify/engine/_plan/refresh_lifecycle.py`):

**The cycle is:** `scan -> review -> workflow -> triage -> execute -> scan`

**"Cleared" is determined by absence, not completion:**
- The queue is "cleared" when `queue_order` becomes empty (all items resolved, skipped, or superseded)
- Once cleared, the system automatically enters the **postflight scan phase**
- `postflight_scan_pending()` returns `True` when a scan hasn't completed yet at the current scan boundary
- The mark is: `plan["refresh_state"]["postflight_scan_completed_at_scan_count"]` = integer scan count

**The progression chain:**
```
1. If objective items exist → LIFECYCLE_PHASE_EXECUTE
2. Else if initial subjective reviews pending → LIFECYCLE_PHASE_REVIEW
3. Else if deferred disposition exists → LIFECYCLE_PHASE_SCAN
4. Else if postflight scan pending → LIFECYCLE_PHASE_SCAN
5. Else if postflight non-objective items exist → LIFECYCLE_PHASE_REVIEW
6. Else if workflow items exist → LIFECYCLE_PHASE_WORKFLOW
7. Else if triage stages pending → LIFECYCLE_PHASE_TRIAGE
8. Else → default to LIFECYCLE_PHASE_SCAN
```

**Key point:** All phases are re-resolved dynamically from current queue items as a "safety net" — the persisted phase state is not blindly trusted.

---

### 2. **What `postflight_scan_pending` Considers "Done"**

From `/desloppify/engine/_plan/refresh_lifecycle.py`, lines 125-130:

```python
def postflight_scan_pending(plan: PlanModel) -> bool:
    """Return True when the current empty-queue boundary still needs a scan."""
    refresh_state = plan.get("refresh_state")
    if not isinstance(refresh_state, dict):
        return True  # No state = scan needed
    return not isinstance(refresh_state.get(_POSTFLIGHT_SCAN_KEY), int)
```

**"Done" criteria:**
- `plan["refresh_state"]["postflight_scan_completed_at_scan_count"]` is set to an integer
- That integer matches the current scan count (ensures freshness across scans)
- If the postflight scan key is absent or not an integer → **scan is pending**

**Lifecycle phase gates on this:**
- Lines 55-56, 111: If `postflight_scan_pending()` is `True`, the phase **stays** in `LIFECYCLE_PHASE_SCAN`
- Queue cannot progress to other phases until this boundary scan completes

---

### 3. **How Scores Treat Queue vs Backlog Items**

**Critical finding: Scoring is independent of queue membership.**

From `/desloppify/engine/_scoring/results/core.py` and `/desloppify/engine/_scoring/results/health.py`:

- Scores are computed from **all open issues in state**, regardless of whether they're in `queue_order`
- The scoring pipeline (lines 38-158 in core.py) takes:
  - `issues: dict` — the full state issues collection
  - `potentials: dict[str, int]` — detector counts (also state-wide)
  - No filtering by queue membership occurs

**Example:** If a detector has 10 open issues but only 3 are in `queue_order`:
- All 10 issues count toward the score
- Only 3 appear in the execution queue
- Score reflects the full codebase health, not the "committed work"

**Backlog items DO affect scores:**
- `compute_subjective_visibility()` (lines 79-137 in `/desloppify/engine/_plan/policy/subjective.py`) computes `objective_count` from **all open non-subjective issues**
- BUT: This policy object gates **queue membership behavior**, not scoring
- The policy's `should_inject_to_plan()` / `should_evict_from_plan()` methods decide whether subjective dimensions enter `queue_order`

---

### 4. **The Triage Workflow — Promoting Items from Backlog to Queue**

**User promotion mechanism:**

From `/desloppify/engine/_plan/operations/queue.py`, the `move_items()` function (lines 94-135):

```python
def move_items(
    plan: PlanModel,
    issue_ids: list[str],
    position: str,
    target: str | None = None,
    offset: int | None = None,
) -> int:
    """Move issue IDs to a position in queue_order. Returns count moved."""
    # ... insert at resolved position ...
    if position == "top":
        add_promoted_ids(plan, issue_ids)  # Track as user-promoted
    return len(issue_ids)
```

**Promotion workflow:**
1. **Backlog items** are visible in `build_backlog_queue()` (lines 88-101 in `/desloppify/engine/planning/queue_policy.py`)
   - Filtered by `visibility=QueueVisibility.BACKLOG` — items NOT in `queue_order` and not implicit workflow
2. **User promotes via:** `desloppify plan move <issue-id> top`
   - Inserts into `queue_order` and tracks in `promoted_ids`
3. **Triage auto-generates clusters:**
   - Epic clusters created/updated in `_upsert_triage_clusters()` (lines 109-133 in `/desloppify/engine/_plan/triage/apply.py`)
   - Issues from epics are ordered into `queue_order` by `_reorder_queue_by_dependency()` (lines 136-150)
4. **Auto-clusters manage subjective items:**
   - `sync_subjective_dimensions()` automatically injects/evicts subjective IDs from `queue_order` based on scoring state
   - Non-objective post-review items are similarly managed

**Key distinction:** Triage creates the **epic/cluster structure** (plan.clusters), but the actual **queue_order insertion** is separate and user-driven or auto-policy-driven.

---

### 5. **How `compute_subjective_visibility` Distinguishes Queue vs Backlog**

From `/desloppify/engine/_plan/policy/subjective.py`, lines 79-137:

```python
def compute_subjective_visibility(
    state: StateModel,
    *,
    target_strict: float = DEFAULT_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE,
    scan_path: ScanPathPolicyOption = _SCAN_PATH_FROM_STATE_POLICY,
    plan: dict | None = None,
) -> SubjectiveVisibility:
    # Count open, non-suppressed, objective issues excluding evidence-only
    objective_count = sum(
        1
        for issue_id, issue in issues.items()
        if issue.get("status") == Status.OPEN
        and issue.get("detector") not in NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS
        and not issue.get("suppressed")
        and not _is_evidence_only(issue)
        and issue_in_scan_scope(str(issue.get("file", "")), resolved_scan_path)
        and issue_id not in skipped_ids  # Plan-skipped excluded
    )
```

**What it DOES distinguish:**
- `has_objective_backlog: bool` — True if any open objective (non-subjective) issues exist
- Respects `plan["skipped"]` — removes plan-skipped issues from count
- **Does NOT separate queue_order from unqueued items** — it counts all open issues

**The policy's role (lines 35-51):**
```python
def should_inject_to_plan(self, fid: str) -> bool:
    """Should this subjective ID be injected into plan queue_order?"""
    if fid in self.unscored_ids:
        return True  # unconditional
    if fid in self.stale_ids:
        return not self.has_objective_backlog  # defer if objective work remains
    if fid in self.under_target_ids:
        return not self.has_objective_backlog  # defer if objective work remains
    return False
```

**This means:**
- If backlog has objective items, subjective work is deferred (not injected into queue_order)
- If backlog is cleared, stale/under-target subjective items are promoted to queue
- BUT: Both backlog AND queue items affect the overall score equally

---

### 6. **Critical Answer to Your Final Question**

**If auto-cluster items were NOT in queue_order, would the queue appear "cleared"?**

**YES. The queue appears cleared when `queue_order` is empty, regardless of what exists in the backlog or in `plan.clusters`.**

**Would scores still account for them?**

**YES. Scores would still reflect all issues in state, including those in unenqueued clusters.**

**Proof:** 
- Queue lifecycle (lines 141-162 in `lifecycle.py`) re-resolves phase from current `items`
- If all items are filtered out by visibility, `_has_objective_items()` returns False
- Then progression continues regardless of what's in `clusters` or backlog
- But `compute_score_bundle()` uses the full state issues dict, not the queue

**Practical implication:**
- An epic cluster with issues NOT in `queue_order` is "invisible to queue lifecycle"
- But those issues still drag down the score
- This is by design: the queue is a UX surface, not the scoring ground truth

1→"""Unified subjective-visibility policy.
     2→
     3→A single frozen dataclass computed once per operation replaces the scattered
     4→``has_objective_items`` / ``objective_count`` computations in
     5→``stale_dimensions`` and ``auto_cluster``.

     7→
     8→from __future__ import annotations
     9→
    10→from dataclasses import dataclass
    11→
    12→from desloppify.base.config import DEFAULT_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE
    13→from desloppify.base.enums import Status
    14→from desloppify.base.registry import DETECTORS
    15→from desloppify.engine._state.filtering import issue_in_scan_scope
    16→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import StateModel
    17→from desloppify.engine.planning.helpers import CONFIDENCE_ORDER
    18→
    19→# Detectors whose issues are NOT objective mechanical work.
    20→NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS: frozenset[str] = frozenset({
    21→    "review", "concerns", "subjective_review", "subjective_assessment",
    22→})
    23→
    24→
    25→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    26→class SubjectiveVisibility:
    27→    """Immutable snapshot of the subjective-vs-objective balance."""
    28→
    29→    has_objective_backlog: bool  # any open non-subjective issues?
    30→    objective_count: int  # how many
    31→    unscored_ids: frozenset[str]  # subjective::* IDs needing initial review
    32→    stale_ids: frozenset[str]  # subjective::* IDs needing re-review
    33→    under_target_ids: frozenset[str]  # below target, not stale/unscored
    34→
    35→    def should_inject_to_plan(self, fid: str) -> bool:
    36→        """Should this subjective ID be injected into plan queue_order?"""
    37→        if fid in self.unscored_ids:
    38→            return True  # unconditional
    39→        if fid in self.stale_ids:
    40→            return not self.has_objective_backlog
    41→        if fid in self.under_target_ids:
    42→            return not self.has_objective_backlog
    43→        return False
    44→
    45→    def should_evict_from_plan(self, fid: str) -> bool:
    46→        """Should this subjective ID be removed from plan queue_order?"""
    47→        if fid in self.unscored_ids:
    48→            return False  # never evict unscored
    49→        if fid in self.stale_ids or fid in self.under_target_ids:
    50→            return self.has_objective_backlog
    51→        return False
    52→
    53→    @property
    54→    def backlog_blocks_rerun(self) -> bool:
    55→        """Preflight: should reruns be blocked?"""
    56→        return self.has_objective_backlog
    57→
    58→
    59→def _is_evidence_only(issue: dict) -> bool:
    60→    """Return True if the issue is below its detector's standalone threshold."""
    61→    detector = issue.get("detector", "")
    62→    meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
    63→    if meta and meta.standalone_threshold:
    64→        threshold_rank = CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(meta.standalone_threshold, 9)
    65→        issue_rank = CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(issue.get("confidence", "low"), 9)
    66→        if issue_rank > threshold_rank:
    67→            return True
    68→    return False
    69→
    70→
    71→class _ScanPathFromStatePolicy:
    72→    """Sentinel type: resolve scan_path from state."""
    73→
    74→
    75→_SCAN_PATH_FROM_STATE_POLICY = _ScanPathFromStatePolicy()
    76→ScanPathPolicyOption = str | None | _ScanPathFromStatePolicy
    77→
    78→
    79→def compute_subjective_visibility(
    80→    state: StateModel,
    81→    *,
    82→    target_strict: float = DEFAULT_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE,
    83→    scan_path: ScanPathPolicyOption = _SCAN_PATH_FROM_STATE_POLICY,
    84→    plan: dict | None = None,
    85→) -> SubjectiveVisibility:
    86→    """Build the policy snapshot from current state.
    87→
    88→    *scan_path* defaults to ``state["scan_path"]`` so callers don't need to
    89→    thread it manually.  Pass an explicit ``str`` to override, or ``None``
    90→    to disable scope filtering.  When *plan* is set, issues whose IDs
    91→    appear in ``plan["skipped"]`` are excluded.
    92→
    93→    Imports policy helpers from ``stale_policy`` so this module remains
    94→    side-effect free and cycle-safe.
    95→    """
    96→    from desloppify.engine._plan.policy.stale import (
    97→        current_stale_ids,
    98→        current_under_target_ids,
    99→        current_unscored_ids,
   100→    )
   101→
   102→    resolved_scan_path: str | None = (
   103→        state.get("scan_path")
   104→        if isinstance(scan_path, _ScanPathFromStatePolicy)
   105→        else scan_path
   106→    )
   107→
   108→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
   109→    skipped_ids = set((plan or {}).get("skipped", {}).keys())
   110→
   111→    # Count open, non-suppressed, objective issues.
   112→    # Evidence-only issues (below standalone confidence threshold) are
   113→    # excluded — they still affect scores but are not actionable queue items.
   114→    # Issues outside scan_path and plan-skipped issues are also excluded
   115→    # so the policy matches what the user actually sees in the queue.
   116→    objective_count = sum(
   117→        1
   118→        for issue_id, issue in issues.items()
   119→        if issue.get("status") == Status.OPEN
   120→        and issue.get("detector") not in NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS
   121→        and not issue.get("suppressed")
   122→        and not _is_evidence_only(issue)
   123→        and issue_in_scan_scope(str(issue.get("file", "")), resolved_scan_path)
   124→        and issue_id not in skipped_ids
   125→    )
   126→
   127→    unscored = current_unscored_ids(state)
   128→    stale = current_stale_ids(state)
   129→    under_target = current_under_target_ids(state, target_strict=target_strict)
   130→
   131→    return SubjectiveVisibility(
   132→        has_objective_backlog=objective_count > 0,
   133→        objective_count=objective_count,
   134→        unscored_ids=frozenset(unscored),
   135→        stale_ids=frozenset(stale),
   136→        under_target_ids=frozenset(under_target),
   137→    )
   138→
   139→
   140→__all__ = [
   141→    "NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS",
   142→    "SubjectiveVisibility",
   143→    "compute_subjective_visibility",
   144→]

1→"""Shared triage-start policy used by sync and command entrypoints."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from dataclasses import dataclass
     6→from typing import Literal
     7→
     8→from desloppify.engine._plan.constants import (
     9→    TRIAGE_IDS,
    10→    recorded_unconfirmed_triage_stage_names,
    11→)
    12→from desloppify.engine._plan.schema import PlanModel
    13→from desloppify.engine._plan.policy.subjective import SubjectiveVisibility
    14→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import StateModel
    15→
    16→from .context import has_objective_backlog, is_mid_cycle
    17→
    18→TriageStartAction = Literal["inject", "defer", "already_active"]
    19→
    20→
    21→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    22→class TriageStartDecision:
    23→    action: TriageStartAction
    24→    reason: str
    25→
    26→
    27→def _has_unfinished_stage_records(plan: PlanModel) -> bool:
    28→    """True when stage reports exist but are still unconfirmed."""
    29→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
    30→    triage_stages = (
    31→        meta.get("triage_stages", {})
    32→        if isinstance(meta, dict)
    33→        else {}
    34→    )
    35→    return bool(recorded_unconfirmed_triage_stage_names(triage_stages))
    36→
    37→
    38→def decide_triage_start(
    39→    plan: PlanModel,
    40→    state: StateModel | dict | None,
    41→    *,
    42→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
    43→    explicit_start: bool = False,
    44→    attested_override: bool = False,
    45→) -> TriageStartDecision:
    46→    """Return whether triage should inject now, defer, or is already active."""
    47→    order = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
    48→    if order & TRIAGE_IDS:
    49→        return TriageStartDecision(action="already_active", reason="already_active")
    50→    if _has_unfinished_stage_records(plan):
    51→        if explicit_start and attested_override:
    52→            return TriageStartDecision(action="inject", reason="attested_override")
    53→        return TriageStartDecision(
    54→            action="defer",
    55→            reason="unfinished_triage_stage_records",
    56→        )
    57→
    58→    if state is None:
    59→        return TriageStartDecision(action="inject", reason="no_state_available")
    60→
    61→    if is_mid_cycle(plan) and has_objective_backlog(state, policy):
    62→        if explicit_start and attested_override:
    63→            return TriageStartDecision(action="inject", reason="attested_override")
    64→        return TriageStartDecision(action="defer", reason="objective_backlog_mid_cycle")
    65→
    66→    return TriageStartDecision(action="inject", reason="default")
    67→
    68→
    69→__all__ = ["TriageStartAction", "TriageStartDecision", "decide_triage_start"]
    70→

1→"""Lifecycle visibility filtering for work-queue items.
     2→
     3→The queue has one explicit cycle:
     4→``scan -> review -> workflow -> triage -> execute -> scan``.
     5→
     6→Two details matter:
     7→- ``review`` can be entered either from a fresh scan with initial subjective
     8→  assessment placeholders, or after execute drains and post-flight review work
     9→  exists. The phase name is the same, but the visible items differ.
    10→- deferred disposition is treated as a blocker inside the ``scan`` boundary.
    11→  It must be cleared before the scan step is considered available.
    12→"""

    14→from __future__ import annotations
    15→
    16→from desloppify.engine.plan_queue import (
    17→    current_lifecycle_phase,
    18→    LIFECYCLE_PHASE_EXECUTE,

    34→
    35→def _validate_postflight_non_objective_detectors() -> None:
    36→    missing = POSTFLIGHT_NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS - NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS
    37→    if missing:
    38→        raise RuntimeError(
    39→            "POSTFLIGHT_NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS has items not in NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS: "
    40→            f"{missing}"
    41→        )
    42→
    43→
    44→_validate_postflight_non_objective_detectors()
    45→
    46→
    47→def _has_objective_items(items: list[WorkQueueItem]) -> bool:
    48→    """True if any objective mechanical work items remain in the queue.
    49→
    50→    Checks both individual issues and collapsed clusters — clusters
    51→    contain objective issues grouped by the queue builder.
    52→    """
    53→    return any(
    54→        item.get("kind") in ("issue", "cluster")
    55→        and item.get("detector", "") not in NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS
    56→        for item in items

    58→

    60→def _has_initial_reviews(items: list[WorkQueueItem]) -> bool:

    63→        item.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension"

    67→
    68→
    69→def _is_postflight_non_objective_item(item: WorkQueueItem) -> bool:
    70→    """True if this item belongs to the non-objective post-flight review phase."""
    71→    if item.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension":

    74→
    75→
    76→def _has_postflight_non_objective_items(items: list[WorkQueueItem]) -> bool:
    77→    """True if any non-objective post-flight review items are pending."""
    78→    return any(_is_postflight_non_objective_item(item) for item in items)
    79→
    80→
    81→def _has_triage_stages(items: list[WorkQueueItem]) -> bool:

    83→    return any(
    84→        item.get("kind") == "workflow_stage"
    85→        and str(item.get("id", "")).startswith("triage::")
    86→        for item in items
    87→    )
    88→
    89→
    90→def _is_deferred_disposition(item: WorkQueueItem) -> bool:

    92→
    93→
    94→def _has_deferred_disposition(items: list[WorkQueueItem]) -> bool:
    95→    return any(_is_deferred_disposition(item) for item in items)
    96→
    97→
    98→def _is_postflight_scan(item: WorkQueueItem) -> bool:
    99→    return item.get("id") == WORKFLOW_RUN_SCAN_ID
   100→
   101→
   102→def _has_postflight_scan(items: list[WorkQueueItem]) -> bool:
   103→    return any(_is_postflight_scan(item) for item in items)
   104→
   105→
   106→def _is_triage_stage(item: WorkQueueItem) -> bool:
   107→    """True when item is a triage workflow stage."""
   108→    return (
   109→        item.get("kind") == "workflow_stage"
   110→        and str(item.get("id", "")).startswith("triage::")

   112→
   113→
   114→def _is_postflight_workflow(item: WorkQueueItem) -> bool:
   115→    return (
   116→        item.get("kind") == "workflow_action"
   117→        and not _is_deferred_disposition(item)
   118→        and not _is_postflight_scan(item)
   119→    )
   120→
   121→
   122→def _has_postflight_workflow(items: list[WorkQueueItem]) -> bool:
   123→    return any(_is_postflight_workflow(item) for item in items)
   124→
   125→
   126→def _is_force_visible(item: WorkQueueItem) -> bool:
   127→    """True when the item is explicitly escalated past objective gating."""
   128→    return bool(item.get("force_visible"))
   129→
   130→
   131→def _is_postflight_phase_item(item: WorkQueueItem) -> bool:
   132→    return (
   133→        _is_postflight_non_objective_item(item)
   134→        or _is_triage_stage(item)
   135→        or _is_deferred_disposition(item)
   136→        or _is_postflight_scan(item)
   137→        or _is_postflight_workflow(item)
   138→    )
   139→
   140→
   141→def resolve_lifecycle_phase(
   142→    items: list[WorkQueueItem],
   143→    *,
   144→    plan: dict | None = None,
   145→) -> str:
   146→    """Resolve the active queue lifecycle phase from current items + plan state."""
   147→    if _has_initial_reviews(items):
   148→        return LIFECYCLE_PHASE_REVIEW
   149→    if _has_objective_items(items):
   150→        return LIFECYCLE_PHASE_EXECUTE
   151→    if _has_deferred_disposition(items) or _has_postflight_scan(items):
   152→        return LIFECYCLE_PHASE_SCAN
   153→    if _has_postflight_non_objective_items(items):
   154→        return LIFECYCLE_PHASE_REVIEW
   155→    if _has_postflight_workflow(items):
   156→        return LIFECYCLE_PHASE_WORKFLOW
   157→    if _has_triage_stages(items):
   158→        return LIFECYCLE_PHASE_TRIAGE
   159→    persisted = current_lifecycle_phase(plan) if isinstance(plan, dict) else None
   160→    if persisted is not None:
   161→        return persisted
   162→    return LIFECYCLE_PHASE_SCAN
   163→
   164→
   165→def apply_lifecycle_filter(
   166→    items: list[WorkQueueItem],
   167→    *,
   168→    plan: dict | None = None,
   169→) -> list[WorkQueueItem]:
   170→    """Enforce lifecycle visibility rules from the resolved explicit phase."""
   171→    phase = resolve_lifecycle_phase(items, plan=plan)
   172→
   173→    if phase == LIFECYCLE_PHASE_REVIEW:
   174→        if _has_initial_reviews(items):
   175→            return [
   176→                item for item in items
   177→                if item.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension" and item.get("initial_review")
   178→            ]
   179→        return [
   180→            item for item in items
   181→            if _is_postflight_non_objective_item(item) or _is_force_visible(item)
   182→        ]
   183→
   184→    if phase == LIFECYCLE_PHASE_EXECUTE:
   185→        return [
   186→            item for item in items
   187→            if not _is_postflight_phase_item(item) or _is_force_visible(item)
   188→        ]
   189→
   190→    if phase == LIFECYCLE_PHASE_SCAN:
   191→        if _has_deferred_disposition(items):
   192→            return [
   193→                item for item in items
   194→                if _is_deferred_disposition(item) or _is_force_visible(item)
   195→            ]
   196→        return [
   197→            item for item in items
   198→            if _is_postflight_scan(item) or _is_force_visible(item)
   199→        ]
   200→
   201→    if phase == LIFECYCLE_PHASE_WORKFLOW:
   202→        return [
   203→            item for item in items
   204→            if _is_postflight_workflow(item) or _is_force_visible(item)
   205→        ]
   206→
   207→    if phase == LIFECYCLE_PHASE_TRIAGE:
   208→        return [item for item in items if _is_triage_stage(item) or _is_force_visible(item)]
   209→
   210→    # Explicit post-flight scan phase without an item should fall back to empty.
   211→    if _has_postflight_scan(items):
   212→        return [
   213→            item for item in items
   214→            if _is_postflight_scan(item) or _is_force_visible(item)
   215→        ]
   216→    return []

    96→    meta = refresh_state.get(_PENDING_IMPORT_SCORES_KEY)
    97→    if isinstance(meta, dict) and meta:
    98→        return meta
    99→    issues_only_audit = _latest_assessment_audit(state, modes={"issues_only"})
   100→    if issues_only_audit is None:
   101→        return None
   102→    return _build_pending_import_scores_meta(
   103→        import_file=str(issues_only_audit.get("import_file", "")),
   104→        import_payload=None,
   105→        issues_only_audit=issues_only_audit,
   106→    )

   108→
   109→def import_scores_meta_matches(
   110→    meta: dict[str, Any] | None,
   111→    *,
   112→    import_file: str,
   113→    import_payload: dict[str, Any],
   114→) -> tuple[bool, str]:
   115→    """Return (matches, reason) for whether the import matches the pending batch.
   116→
   117→    Checks packet_sha256 first (strongest signal), falls back to normalized
   118→    file path.  Returns a single human-readable reason on mismatch.
   119→    """
   120→    if not isinstance(meta, dict) or not meta:
   121→        return True, ""
   122→
   123→    provenance = import_payload.get("provenance")
   124→    provenance_dict = provenance if isinstance(provenance, dict) else {}
   125→
   126→    expected_hash = str(meta.get("packet_sha256", "")).strip()
   127→    current_hash = str(provenance_dict.get("packet_sha256", "")).strip()
   128→    if expected_hash and current_hash:
   129→        if current_hash == expected_hash:
   130→            return True, ""
   131→        return False, f"expected packet_sha256 {expected_hash}, got {current_hash}"
   132→
   133→    expected_file = str(meta.get("normalized_import_file", "")).strip()
   134→    current_file = _normalize_match_path(import_file) or ""
   135→    if expected_file and current_file and current_file != expected_file:
   136→        return False, f"expected import file {meta.get('import_file')}, got {import_file}"
   137→
   138→    return True, ""
   139→
   140→
   141→def _clear_pending_import_scores(plan: PlanModel) -> None:
   142→    order = plan["queue_order"]
   143→    if WORKFLOW_IMPORT_SCORES_ID in order:
   144→        order[:] = [item for item in order if item != WORKFLOW_IMPORT_SCORES_ID]
   145→    refresh_state = _refresh_state(plan)
   146→    refresh_state.pop(_PENDING_IMPORT_SCORES_KEY, None)
   147→
   148→
   149→def _pending_compare_timestamp(
   150→    pending_meta: dict[str, Any] | None,
   151→    latest_issues_only: dict[str, Any],
   152→) -> str:
   153→    if isinstance(pending_meta, dict):
   154→        pending_ts = str(pending_meta.get("timestamp", "")).strip()
   155→        if pending_ts:
   156→            return pending_ts
   157→    return str(latest_issues_only.get("timestamp", "")).strip()
   158→
   159→
   160→def _pending_import_scores_stale(
   161→    *,
   162→    order: list[str],
   163→    pending_meta: dict[str, Any] | None,
   164→    latest_issues_only: dict[str, Any] | None,
   165→    latest_trusted: dict[str, Any] | None,
   166→) -> bool:
   167→    if WORKFLOW_IMPORT_SCORES_ID not in order:
   168→        return False
   169→    if latest_issues_only is None:
   170→        return True
   171→    if latest_trusted is None:
   172→        return False
   173→
   174→    latest_trusted_ts = str(latest_trusted.get("timestamp", "")).strip()
   175→    compare_ts = _pending_compare_timestamp(pending_meta, latest_issues_only)
   176→    return bool(compare_ts and latest_trusted_ts and latest_trusted_ts >= compare_ts)
   177→
   178→
   179→def _record_pending_import_scores(
   180→    refresh_state: dict[str, Any],
   181→    *,
   182→    import_file: str | None,
   183→    import_payload: dict[str, Any] | None,
   184→    latest_issues_only: dict[str, Any] | None,
   185→) -> None:
   186→    refresh_state[_PENDING_IMPORT_SCORES_KEY] = _build_pending_import_scores_meta(
   187→        import_file=import_file,
   188→        import_payload=import_payload,
   189→        issues_only_audit=latest_issues_only,
   190→    )

   192→
   193→def _no_unscored(
   194→    state: StateModel,
   195→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None,

   198→    if policy is not None:

   200→    return not stale_policy_mod.current_unscored_ids(
   201→        state, subjective_prefix=SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX,

   205→def _inject(plan: PlanModel, item_id: str) -> QueueSyncResult:
   206→    """Inject *item_id* into the workflow prefix and clear stale skip entries."""
   207→    order = plan["queue_order"]
   208→    if item_id not in order:
   209→        order.append(item_id)
   210→    normalize_queue_workflow_and_triage_prefix(order)
   211→    skipped = plan.get("skipped", {})
   212→    if isinstance(skipped, dict):
   213→        skipped.pop(item_id, None)
   214→    return QueueSyncResult(injected=[item_id])
   215→
   216→
   217→_EMPTY = QueueSyncResult
   218→
   219→
   220→def sync_score_checkpoint_needed(
   221→    plan: PlanModel,
   222→    state: StateModel,
   223→    *,
   224→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
   225→) -> QueueSyncResult:
   226→    """Inject ``workflow::score-checkpoint`` when all initial reviews complete.
   227→

   229→    - No unscored (placeholder) subjective dimensions remain
   230→    - ``workflow::score-checkpoint`` is not already in the queue
   231→
   232→    Front-loads it into the workflow prefix so it stays ahead of triage.
   233→    """
   234→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   235→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   236→
   237→    if WORKFLOW_SCORE_CHECKPOINT_ID in order:
   238→        return _EMPTY()
   239→    if not _no_unscored(state, policy):

   244→def sync_create_plan_needed(
   245→    plan: PlanModel,
   246→    state: StateModel,
   247→    *,
   248→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
   249→) -> QueueSyncResult:
   250→    """Inject ``workflow::create-plan`` when reviews complete + objective backlog exists.
   251→
   252→    Only injects when:
   253→    - No unscored (placeholder) subjective dimensions remain
   254→    - At least one objective issue exists
   255→    - ``workflow::create-plan`` is not already in the queue
   256→    - No triage stages are pending
   257→
   258→    Front-loads it into the workflow prefix so it stays ahead of triage.
   259→    """
   260→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   261→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   262→
   263→    if WORKFLOW_CREATE_PLAN_ID in order:
   264→        return _EMPTY()
   265→    if any(sid in order for sid in TRIAGE_IDS):
   266→        return _EMPTY()
   267→    if not _no_unscored(state, policy):
   268→        return _EMPTY()
   269→
   270→    if not has_objective_backlog(state, policy):
   271→        return _EMPTY()

   273→    return _inject(plan, WORKFLOW_CREATE_PLAN_ID)
   274→
   275→
   276→def sync_import_scores_needed(
   277→    plan: PlanModel,
   278→    state: StateModel,
   279→    *,
   280→    assessment_mode: str | None = None,
   281→    import_file: str | None = None,
   282→    import_payload: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   283→) -> QueueSyncResult:
   284→    """Inject ``workflow::import-scores`` after issues-only import.
   285→
   286→    Only injects when:
   287→    - Assessment mode was ``issues_only`` (scores were skipped)
   288→    - ``workflow::import-scores`` is not already in the queue
   289→
   290→    Front-loads it into the workflow prefix so it stays ahead of triage.
   291→    """
   292→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   293→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   294→    refresh_state = _refresh_state(plan)
   295→    pending_meta = refresh_state.get(_PENDING_IMPORT_SCORES_KEY)
   296→    latest_issues_only = _latest_assessment_audit(state, modes={"issues_only"})
   297→    latest_trusted = _latest_assessment_audit(state, modes=_TRUSTED_ASSESSMENT_MODES)
   298→
   299→    if _pending_import_scores_stale(
   300→        order=order,
   301→        pending_meta=pending_meta,
   302→        latest_issues_only=latest_issues_only,
   303→        latest_trusted=latest_trusted,
   304→    ):
   305→        _clear_pending_import_scores(plan)
   306→        return QueueSyncResult(pruned=[WORKFLOW_IMPORT_SCORES_ID])
   307→
   308→    if WORKFLOW_IMPORT_SCORES_ID in order:
   309→        if assessment_mode == "issues_only":
   310→            _record_pending_import_scores(
   311→                refresh_state,
   312→                import_file=import_file,
   313→                import_payload=import_payload,
   314→                latest_issues_only=latest_issues_only,
   315→            )
   316→            return QueueSyncResult(resurfaced=[WORKFLOW_IMPORT_SCORES_ID])
   317→        return _EMPTY()
   318→    if assessment_mode != "issues_only":
   319→        return _EMPTY()
   320→    result = _inject(plan, WORKFLOW_IMPORT_SCORES_ID)
   321→    _record_pending_import_scores(
   322→        refresh_state,
   323→        import_file=import_file,
   324→        import_payload=import_payload,
   325→        latest_issues_only=latest_issues_only,
   326→    )
   327→    return result

   330→class ScoreSnapshot:
   331→    """Minimal score snapshot for rebaseline — avoids importing state.py."""
   332→
   333→    __slots__ = ("strict", "overall", "objective", "verified")
   334→
   335→    def __init__(
   336→        self,
   337→        *,
   338→        strict: float | None,
   339→        overall: float | None,
   340→        objective: float | None,
   341→        verified: float | None,
   342→    ) -> None:
   343→        self.strict = strict
   344→        self.overall = overall
   345→        self.objective = objective
   346→        self.verified = verified
   347→
   348→
   349→def sync_communicate_score_needed(
   350→    plan: PlanModel,
   351→    state: StateModel,
   352→    *,
   353→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
   354→    scores_just_imported: bool = False,
   355→    current_scores: ScoreSnapshot | None = None,
   356→) -> QueueSyncResult:
   357→    """Inject ``workflow::communicate-score`` and rebaseline scores.
   358→
   359→    Injects when:
   360→    - All initial subjective reviews are complete (no unscored dims), OR
   361→      scores were just imported (trusted/attested/override)
   362→    - ``workflow::communicate-score`` is not already in the queue
   363→    - Score has not already been communicated this cycle
   364→      (``previous_plan_start_scores`` absent), unless a trusted score import
   365→      explicitly refreshed the live score mid-cycle
   366→
   367→    When injected and *current_scores* is provided, ``plan_start_scores``
   368→    is rebaselined to the current score so the score display unfreezes at
   369→    the new value.  The previous baseline is preserved in
   370→    ``previous_plan_start_scores`` so the communicate-score queue item can
   371→    show the old → new delta — and so mid-cycle scans know not to
   372→    re-inject.
   373→    """
   374→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   375→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   376→
   377→    if WORKFLOW_COMMUNICATE_SCORE_ID in order:
   378→        return _EMPTY()
   379→    # Already communicated this cycle — previous_plan_start_scores is set
   380→    # at injection time and cleared at cycle boundaries.
   381→    if "previous_plan_start_scores" in plan and not scores_just_imported:
   382→        return _EMPTY()
   383→    if not scores_just_imported and not _no_unscored(state, policy):
   384→        return _EMPTY()
   385→
   386→    if current_scores is not None:
   387→        _rebaseline_plan_start_scores(plan, current_scores)
   388→    # Set sentinel even when rebaseline was a no-op (no plan_start_scores
   389→    # to rebaseline) so mid-cycle scans don't re-inject.
   390→    if not plan.get("previous_plan_start_scores"):
   391→        plan["previous_plan_start_scores"] = {}
   392→    return _inject(plan, WORKFLOW_COMMUNICATE_SCORE_ID)
   393→
   394→
   395→def _rebaseline_plan_start_scores(
   396→    plan: PlanModel,
   397→    scores: ScoreSnapshot,
   398→) -> None:
   399→    """Snapshot the current score as the new baseline, preserving the old one."""
   400→    old_start = plan.get("plan_start_scores")
   401→    if not isinstance(old_start, dict) or not old_start:
   402→        return
   403→    if scores.strict is None:
   404→        return
   405→
   406→    plan["previous_plan_start_scores"] = dict(old_start)
   407→    plan["plan_start_scores"] = {
   408→        "strict": scores.strict,
   409→        "overall": scores.overall,
   410→        "objective": scores.objective,
   411→        "verified": scores.verified,
   412→    }
   413→
   414→
   415→__all__ = [
   416→    "ScoreSnapshot",
   417→    "import_scores_meta_matches",
   418→    "pending_import_scores_meta",
   419→    "sync_communicate_score_needed",
   420→    "sync_create_plan_needed",
   421→    "sync_import_scores_needed",
   422→    "sync_score_checkpoint_needed",
   423→]

1→"""Unified subjective-visibility policy.
     2→
     3→A single frozen dataclass computed once per operation replaces the scattered
     4→``has_objective_items`` / ``objective_count`` computations in
     5→``stale_dimensions`` and ``auto_cluster``.
     6→"""
     7→
     8→from __future__ import annotations
     9→
    10→from dataclasses import dataclass
    11→
    12→from desloppify.base.config import DEFAULT_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE
    13→from desloppify.base.enums import Status
    14→from desloppify.base.registry import DETECTORS
    15→from desloppify.engine._state.filtering import issue_in_scan_scope
    16→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import StateModel
    17→from desloppify.engine.planning.helpers import CONFIDENCE_ORDER
    18→
    19→# Detectors whose issues are NOT objective mechanical work.
    20→NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS: frozenset[str] = frozenset({
    21→    "review", "concerns", "subjective_review", "subjective_assessment",
    22→})
    23→
    24→
    25→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    26→class SubjectiveVisibility:
    27→    """Immutable snapshot of the subjective-vs-objective balance."""
    28→
    29→    has_objective_backlog: bool  # any open non-subjective issues?
    30→    objective_count: int  # how many
    31→    unscored_ids: frozenset[str]  # subjective::* IDs needing initial review
    32→    stale_ids: frozenset[str]  # subjective::* IDs needing re-review
    33→    under_target_ids: frozenset[str]  # below target, not stale/unscored
    34→
    35→    def should_inject_to_plan(self, fid: str) -> bool:
    36→        """Should this subjective ID be injected into plan queue_order?"""
    37→        if fid in self.unscored_ids:
    38→            return True  # unconditional
    39→        if fid in self.stale_ids:
    40→            return not self.has_objective_backlog
    41→        if fid in self.under_target_ids:
    42→            return not self.has_objective_backlog
    43→        return False
    44→
    45→    def should_evict_from_plan(self, fid: str) -> bool:
    46→        """Should this subjective ID be removed from plan queue_order?"""
    47→        if fid in self.unscored_ids:
    48→            return False  # never evict unscored
    49→        if fid in self.stale_ids or fid in self.under_target_ids:
    50→            return self.has_objective_backlog
    51→        return False
    52→
    53→    @property
    54→    def backlog_blocks_rerun(self) -> bool:
    55→        """Preflight: should reruns be blocked?"""
    56→        return self.has_objective_backlog
    57→
    58→
    59→def _is_evidence_only(issue: dict) -> bool:
    60→    """Return True if the issue is below its detector's standalone threshold."""
    61→    detector = issue.get("detector", "")
    62→    meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
    63→    if meta and meta.standalone_threshold:
    64→        threshold_rank = CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(meta.standalone_threshold, 9)
    65→        issue_rank = CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(issue.get("confidence", "low"), 9)
    66→        if issue_rank > threshold_rank:
    67→            return True
    68→    return False

    71→class _ScanPathFromStatePolicy:
    72→    """Sentinel type: resolve scan_path from state."""

    75→_SCAN_PATH_FROM_STATE_POLICY = _ScanPathFromStatePolicy()
    76→ScanPathPolicyOption = str | None | _ScanPathFromStatePolicy

    79→def compute_subjective_visibility(
    80→    state: StateModel,
    81→    *,
    82→    target_strict: float = DEFAULT_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE,
    83→    scan_path: ScanPathPolicyOption = _SCAN_PATH_FROM_STATE_POLICY,
    84→    plan: dict | None = None,
    85→) -> SubjectiveVisibility:
    86→    """Build the policy snapshot from current state.
    87→
    88→    *scan_path* defaults to ``state["scan_path"]`` so callers don't need to
    89→    thread it manually.  Pass an explicit ``str`` to override, or ``None``
    90→    to disable scope filtering.  When *plan* is set, issues whose IDs
    91→    appear in ``plan["skipped"]`` are excluded.
    92→
    93→    Imports policy helpers from ``stale_policy`` so this module remains
    94→    side-effect free and cycle-safe.
    95→    """
    96→    from desloppify.engine._plan.policy.stale import (
    97→        current_stale_ids,
    98→        current_under_target_ids,
    99→        current_unscored_ids,
   100→    )
   101→
   102→    resolved_scan_path: str | None = (
   103→        state.get("scan_path")
   104→        if isinstance(scan_path, _ScanPathFromStatePolicy)
   105→        else scan_path
   106→    )
   107→
   108→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
   109→    skipped_ids = set((plan or {}).get("skipped", {}).keys())
   110→
   111→    # Count open, non-suppressed, objective issues.
   112→    # Evidence-only issues (below standalone confidence threshold) are
   113→    # excluded — they still affect scores but are not actionable queue items.
   114→    # Issues outside scan_path and plan-skipped issues are also excluded
   115→    # so the policy matches what the user actually sees in the queue.
   116→    objective_count = sum(
   117→        1
   118→        for issue_id, issue in issues.items()
   119→        if issue.get("status") == Status.OPEN
   120→        and issue.get("detector") not in NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS
   121→        and not issue.get("suppressed")
   122→        and not _is_evidence_only(issue)
   123→        and issue_in_scan_scope(str(issue.get("file", "")), resolved_scan_path)
   124→        and issue_id not in skipped_ids
   125→    )
   126→
   127→    unscored = current_unscored_ids(state)
   128→    stale = current_stale_ids(state)
   129→    under_target = current_under_target_ids(state, target_strict=target_strict)
   130→
   131→    return SubjectiveVisibility(
   132→        has_objective_backlog=objective_count > 0,
   133→        objective_count=objective_count,
   134→        unscored_ids=frozenset(unscored),
   135→        stale_ids=frozenset(stale),
   136→        under_target_ids=frozenset(under_target),
   137→    )
   138→
   139→
   140→__all__ = [
   141→    "NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS",
   142→    "SubjectiveVisibility",
   143→    "compute_subjective_visibility",
   144→]
   145→

     2→
     3→Single-pass sync for all three subjective categories:

     5→- **unscored** — placeholder dimensions never yet reviewed.  Injected at cycle

    85→    keep_ids: set[str],
    86→    pruned: list[str],
    87→) -> None:

    89→    to_remove = [

   102→    if not isinstance(skipped, dict):

   118→    if not skipped_ids:

   120→    to_remove = [fid for fid in order if fid in skipped_ids]
   121→    for fid in to_remove:

   126→def _inject_subjective_ids(

   131→) -> None:
   132→    """Inject subjective IDs into *order* if not already present.
   133→
   134→    Always appends to the back — new items never reorder existing queue.
   135→    """
   136→    existing = set(order)
   137→    for sid in sorted(inject_ids):
   138→        if sid not in existing:
   139→            order.append(sid)
   140→            injected.append(sid)

   143→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   144→# Deferral tracking and escalation
